newsitem.title: UK: Go-Ahead rejects forecast of heavy losses.
newsitem.headline: Go-Ahead rejects forecast of heavy losses.

text.p: UK rail and bus operator Go-Ahead Group Plc on Monday dismissed a report which claimed it and four other transport companies face heavy losses on their rail franchises.

Martin Ballinger, managing director of Go-Ahead -- which owns the Thameslink line operating trains through London from the South Coast to Bedford -- defended the revenue estimates on which his franchise bid was based.

"We stand by the estimates that were prepared by our consultants," Ballinger told Reuters. "They estimate around five percent growth (in revenues) and that's more accurate for the railways we are concerned with."

The report, commissioned by pressure group Save Our Railways (SOR), said five out of the total 25 train operating companies, including Thameslink and three run by Prism Rail Plc, would make losses whatever assumptions were used.
Go-Ahead shares were 14p lower at 485p by 1244 GMT while Prism was down 50p at 305.
SOR used four different assumptions, depending on likely increases in net revenue over the next seven years, as the basis for the study.
It said a further four franchises would run into financial difficulties, though eight -- including Stagecoach Plc's South West Trains -- would make large profits.
"The overall summary suggests they have applied a 1-1/2 percent increase (in revenue) and said on that basis we will make a loss," Ballinger said.
"Unfortunately that doesn't take into account the fact that our Oxford branch, which is called Thames Trains, has had enormous increases in revenue."
